claim.pdf_says: D.6.3   Accessing data and files / D.6.3.1   General / D.6.3.2   Names / D.6.3.3   Items overview / D.6.3.4   Item types / D.6.3.4.1   Working-storage records
claim.markdown_says: ## D.6.3 Accessing data and files / ### D.6.3.1 General / ### D.6.3.2 Names / ## D.6.3.3 Items overview / ## D.6.3.4 Item types / ### D.6.3.4.1 Working-storage records
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown heading level does not track the printed numbering depth, so the outline nests wrongly: D.6.3.3 and D.6.3.4 are emitted at '##', making them siblings of their own parent D.6.3 and of the peer subsections D.6.3.1/D.6.3.2 that are emitted at '###'. The same inversion recurs on every page of this batch (1079: D.6.3.5, D.6.3.6; 1081: D.6.4.4, D.6.5.1-D.6.5.3; 1082: D.6.5.3.1-D.6.5.3.3; 1083: D.6.5.4; 1084: D.6.5.5, D.6.5.6; 1085: D.6.5.6.3; 1086: D.6.5.6.4-D.6.5.6.6; 1087: D.6.5.6.7, D.6.5.6.8, D.6.5.7; 1088: D.6.5.8, D.6.6; 1089: D.7). NO TEXT IS LOST - the clause number in the heading text still encodes the true level - so this is an outline/navigation defect, not a normative one. It is also not specific to these pages: across Annex D a depth-4 number is rendered variously as '##' (26x), '###' (23x) and '####' (2x). Fix with one document-wide pass; do not hand-edit only these twelve pages or the inconsistency simply moves.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED on four independent grounds, each verified directly against a 300 dpi render of the page and against specs/ISO_COBOL.md.

(1) THE KIND LABEL IS FALSE - NOTHING IS MISSING. PDF page 1078 (printed folio 1048) prints exactly seven headings: D.6.3.3 Items overview, D.6.3.4 Item types, D.6.3.4.1 Working-storage records, D.6.3.4.2 File connectors, D.6.3.4.3 Record areas for files, D.6.3.4.4 Screen records, D.6.3.4.5 Other items. All seven appear in specs/ISO_COBOL.md at lines 43255, 43260, 43263, 43268, 43273, 43278 and 43285 with verbatim title text, correct clause numbers, correct order, and a matching <a id="section-..."> anchor apiece. Every body paragraph beneath them is present as well. Not one heading and not one word of text is absent.

(2) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES THE PAGE IT NAMES. Three of the six headings its 'pdf_says' attributes to page 1078 - D.6.3 Accessing data and files, D.6.3.1 General, D.6.3.2 Names - are not on page 1078 at all. I rendered page 1077 (printed folio 1047) and they print there, above the page break. Conversely the quote omits D.6.3.4.2 through D.6.3.4.5, which do print on 1078. Consequently the alleged inversion is not even observable on page 1078: taken on its own, the page-1078 markdown is perfectly self-consistent, mapping both 4-component numbers to '##' and all five 5-component numbers to '###'. The exhibit is a cross-page-break artifact, i.e. page-break furniture, which is an explicit rejection ground.

(3) THE PDF CARRIES NO HEADING-LEVEL SIGNAL FOR THE MARKDOWN TO HAVE LOST. Looking at the printed glyphs on both renders, D.6.3 (depth 3), D.6.3.1/D.6.3.2/D.6.3.3/D.6.3.4 (depth 4) and D.6.3.4.1-D.6.3.4.5 (depth 5) are all set in the same bold serif face, at the same apparent size, flush to the same left margin, with the same number-to-title tab. I confirmed this mechanically with PyMuPDF span metadata rather than trusting the eye: PDF page index 1076 (= page 1077) contains exactly one bold style, Cambria,Bold at 11.67 pt, across 4 spans (running head + D.6.3 + D.6.3.1 + D.6.3.2); PDF page index 1077 (= page 1078) contains exactly one bold style, Cambria,Bold at 11.67 pt, across 8 spans (running head + the seven headings). Body text on both pages is Cambria 10.7 pt. So ISO renders a depth-3, a depth-4 and a depth-5 clause identically; hierarchy is carried solely by the dotted clause number, which the transcription reproduces exactly. The markdown '#' count is an interpolation by the transcriber, not a transcription of anything printed - there is no source-side value it can contradict.

(4) IT FAILS THE STATED REJECTION TESTS ON ITS OWN ADMISSION. The claim concedes 'NO TEXT IS LOST' and 'an outline/navigation defect, not a normative one'. A '##' versus '###' prefix is formatting; it alters no normative content, no requirement, and no COBOL semantics. Differences that are only formatting, or that do not change meaning, are to be rejected.

ONE SUB-ASSERTION SURVIVES, and it is worth recording separately because it is broader than filed: specs/ISO_COBOL.md maps numbering depth to '#' count inconsistently throughout Annex D. Tallying component-count against emitted level over every Annex D heading gives - 2-component (D.x): '##' 30x, '###' 2x; 3-component (D.x.y): '##' 61x, '###' 24x, '####' 2x; 4-component (D.x.y.z): '##' 79x, '###' 48x, '####' 8x; 5-component (D.x.y.z.w): '##' 26x, '###' 23x, '####' 2x. The last row reproduces the claim's 26/23/2 exactly, so the claim's 'depth-4' means a 5-component number. That inconsistency is genuine, but it is a self-consistency defect internal to the markdown, decidable from the clause number alone without ever opening the PDF, spanning well over a hundred headings. It is not a divergence from the canonical source, and filing it twelve times as per-page 'missing-heading / structural' misclassifies a global cosmetic cleanup as per-page content loss.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF/markdown content discrepancy; reject as filed. Every heading printed on page 1078 - D.6.3.3, D.6.3.4, and D.6.3.4.1 through D.6.3.4.5 - is present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md with verbatim text and correct clause numbers, so nothing is missing and the 'missing-heading' kind is wrong. The claim also misattributes D.6.3, D.6.3.1 and D.6.3.2 to page 1078 (they print on page 1077) while omitting D.6.3.4.2-.5 which do print on 1078; the alleged sibling inversion is therefore purely an artifact of straddling the page break, and page 1078's markdown is internally consistent in isolation. PyMuPDF span extraction confirms both pages use exactly one heading style, Cambria,Bold 11.67 pt, irrespective of clause depth, so the PDF supplies no heading-level information beyond the dotted number the markdown already preserves. What is real is a document-wide inconsistency in how specs/ISO_COBOL.md maps numbering depth to '#' count across Annex D (2-component 30/2; 3-component 61/24/2; 4-component 79/48/8; 5-component 26/23/2). If tracked at all it should be re-filed ONCE, scoped document-wide, as a cosmetic/navigational transcription-consistency task - fixed by deriving the level mechanically from the clause number's dot count - not as twelve per-page structural findings against the PDF.
